DutyBack

Getting small importers their struck-down tariffs back,
before the deadlines pass

Vy Bui (vb473) · October 2026

Synthetic sample companies · not legal advice

The problem

$166B in struck-down tariffs. Refunds are not automatic.

330,000+importers paid IEEPA duties on 53M entries
80 daysafter liquidation, CBP's CAPE system stops taking an entry
180 daysafter liquidation, even a protest is too late
  • Every entry has its own clock, so money expires one entry at a time
  • Small firms lag: few had refund accounts set up by April; Congress flagged it in September

CBP declaration to the CIT (Mar 2026) · CSMS #68340863 · 19 U.S.C. 1514 · Atlanta Fed (Sept 2026) · House letter (Sept 9, 2026)

What's not automated

Filing is easy. Sorting is the hard part.

  • A CAPE filing is just a list of entry numbers
  • But each entry needs: liquidation date, 8 exclusion checks, 2 date windows, IEEPA vs Section 301/232 on the same line
  • Spread across 7501s, broker statements, ACE reports, emails, each broker's own layout
  • Brokers and lawyers do it by hand. I found no low-cost tool for small importers.

How it works

Agents read and explain. Code checks and decides.

1. Safety screen
code · drops hidden text and AI-instruction lines, file limits
→
2. Reader agent(s)
Claude · every entry, flag and duty line, each with a quote · big files split and read in parallel
→
3. Verify
code · quotes found? date next to this entry? duty printed and value × rate = duty?
→
4. Checker agent
Claude + 4 read-only tools · finds what's missing or wrong, must quote the documents
5. Repair
Reader re-reads only the flagged entries · code verifies again · never "fixes" without a quote
→
6. Rules engine
code · route, refund, deadline for every entry (CBP rules, snapshot Oct 24, 2026)
→
7. Advisor agent
Claude · plain-English plan + broker email from the engine's results
→
8. Number check + files
code · removes sentences with unknown $, dates, entries · CAPE CSV · calendar

gpt-6-luna on the course key (Claude optional) · strict structured outputs · Checker gets 4 read-only tools · agents have no other tools · cost cap per call

Evidence, not trust

Every number traces to the paperwork

  • Each fact has a quote; code finds it in the PDF
  • A date only counts if it sits next to that entry
  • Printed duty, and value × rate = duty
  • Section 301 and 232 lines never counted as IEEPA
  • Can't verify? It goes to Check by hand, never into the filing

On the course model, one prompt put a wrong entry in the CAPE file and missed 2 deadlines; DutyBack's code checks caught both. On Claude Opus both were perfect in the final run (one prompt missed 2 protest windows the night before). DutyBack's edge: date math in code, evidence for every number, and it fails safe under attack.

Tokenomics

Under 1 cent to sort $73,460 of duty

$0.009Lotus, 13 entries, gpt-6-luna
$0.031Meridian, 48 entries, 6 Readers in parallel
$325/mofor 10,000 users (4 runs of 13 entries each)
  • Same 82/82 accuracy as Claude Opus ($2.57 for the 4 importers) at $0.05
  • Guards: $ cap per call, daily run cap, page limits, Checker turn limit
  • CBP estimates ~5 min per entry by hand; brokers charge ~$200–350/entry (vendor blogs)
Safety

The attacks that broke v1 no longer reach the filing

  • Screen drops invisible text and AI-instruction lines
  • Routes and amounts come from code, not the model
  • Advisor's sentences with unknown $ / dates are removed
  • Red team broke the first version (CAPE file $34.8k → $95.5k); after fixes the file matched the clean run under every attack
  • Never files, never promises a refund, not legal advice
